content:
This is a recently discovered bug. The symptom is that if you previously attached a file, but the previous containing folder now no longer exists because it was deleted or renamed, when you later try to attach a file using the Write window's "Attach" button, it will silently fail. That is, clicking the button will appear to do nothing. The bug should be fixed in the next release.

In the meantime, a workaround is to drag-and-drop the file onto the Write window using the mouse.

Or, if you don't mind changing Thunderbird's Advanced Settings:

- In <Settings | General | Config Editor> search for: "mail.compose.attach.dir".

- The value (path) here must be changed to one that is still available (for example C:\).

- Close and exit Thunderbird, then restart it (this step might not be necessary.)

If this account uses "Normal Password" as its authentication method:

- Go to <Settings | Privacy & Security | Passwords | Saved Passwords>. You can edit your existing password there.

If this account uses "OAuth2" as its authentication method:

- Go to <...Saved Passwords> and delete any entries for that account/user name.

- Go to <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Show Cookies> and delete any cookies from this email provider.

- Make sure the the "Accept Cookies from Sites" option is enabled.

- Restart Thunderbird and you will be prompted for your new credentials.

- What version of Thunderbird?

- What is your operating system?

- What antivirus, Internet security software, or VPN are you using, if any?

- What "3rd parties email servers" are you referring to? That implies to me that there may be a misspelling somewhere, or there's some other program on your computer (like and AV) that's interfering with the connection.

You do have to tell Comcast to "Allow access to my Xfinity Email through third-party programs." That setting at Xfinity's web mail page is found at <Email Settings (gear icon) | Security | Third Party Access Security>.

If Thunderbird can't automatically detect the proper server settings, you should be able to manually enter the correct settings. Here are my working Comcast settings:

MAP (Incoming): Incoming Server Type: IMAP Mail Server Incoming Server Name: imap.comcast.net Port: 993 User Name: <my email address> Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: Normal Password OR OAuth2

SMTP (Outgoing): SMTP Server Name: smtp.comcast.net Port: 465 Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: Normal Password OR OAuth2 User Name: <my email address>

The "special account" is Local Folders. They are for storing messages to your local computer and they have no external account associated with them. This article describes them in more detail. content:
There can be a few reasons for certificate errors like that, including:

- You could be using incorrect server settings in Thunderbird. You should verify them by checking on the provider's help page or contacting the provider's tech support.

- Anti-virus, network security, and VPN programs are notorious for co-opting normal authentication processes. If you use any of those, as a test, try temporarily disabling them or creating an exception for Thunderbird.

- They could, indeed, be having server and/or certificate issues. They may already be aware of it and be working on a fix, so if you were to wait a while it may go away when they do, or you can contact them for status.
